1996.seasonNote: First PGA TOUR season as a professional. Won twice, including his first TOUR victory at the Las Vegas Invitational.

1997.seasonNote: First full season on TOUR. Won the Masters by 12 shots and finished first on Tour with 13 top-10 finishes.

1998.seasonNote: Built on his first full year on TOUR and posted 13 top-10 finishes.

1999.seasonNote: Earned a TOUR-record $6,616,585, nearly $3 million more than his nearest competitor, David Duval.

events.tournament: World Golf Championships-Accenture Match Play Championship

2000.seasonNote: Set or tied 27 PGA TOUR records. Won the U.S. Open, The Open Championship and PGA Championship while completing the career Grand Slam.
2000.seasonFact: Finished with a scoring average of 68.17 and earned a then-record $9.19 million.

events.tournament: World Golf Championships-Accenture Match Play Championship
National Car Rental Golf Classic Disney

2001.seasonNote: Won Player of the Year honors for the third consecutive year and fourth time in five seasons. Led TOUR in Scoring Average (68.81 adjusted) for the third straight year and captured his third straight Vardon Trophy. Earned five TOUR titles and did not miss a cut in 19 starts.
2001.seasonFact: Completed the Tiger Slam by winning the Masters while holding all four major titles at once.

events.tournament: National Car Rental Golf Classic Disney

2002.seasonNote: Led the PGA TOUR in earnings and was named Player of the Year for the fourth consecutive season and the fifth time in six years.
2002.seasonFact: Won the Masters and U.S. Open in the same season.

2005.seasonFact: Became the first player in PGA TOUR history to earn more than $10 million in a single season, finishing with over $10.6 million in official earnings.

2006.seasonFact: Won six straight PGA TOUR starts from The Open Championship through the World Golf Championships-American Express Championship.

2007.seasonFact: Became the first player to earn more than $10 million in official PGA TOUR earnings twice, finishing the season with over $10.8 million.
